results.name: single_digit_targets_after_two_digit_sets
results.description: Among sets whose examples are all two-digit (10-99), yes rate for single-digit targets (1-9) minus other non-example targets of 10-99; observed below null means people treat single-digit numbers as a category excluded by two-digit examples more than the model predicts, above null means they accept them more.
results.code:
# name: single_digit_targets_after_two_digit_sets
# description: Among sets whose examples are all two-digit (10-99), yes rate for single-digit targets (1-9) minus other non-example targets of 10-99; observed below null means people treat single-digit numbers as a category excluded by two-digit examples more than the model predicts, above null means they accept them more.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").values
    e = np.nan_to_num(ex, nan=50)
    two = ((e >= 10) & (e <= 99)).all(1)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values
    isex = (ex == t[:, None]).any(1)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    m = two & ~isex
    a = r[m & (t <= 9)]; b = r[m & (t >= 10) & (t <= 99)]
    if len(a) == 0 or len(b) == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(a.mean() - b.mean())

results.name: participant_yes_rate_spread_same_design
results.description: SD of participant yes rates around the mean of participants who saw the same stimuli (participants delimited by trial_index restarts, design group = first set seen); observed above null means real individual differences in yes-bias the pooled model lacks, below null means participants are more homogeneous than binomial noise.
results.code:
# name: participant_yes_rate_spread_same_design
# description: SD of participant yes rates around the mean of participants who saw the same stimuli (participants delimited by trial_index restarts, design group = first set seen); observed above null means real individual differences in yes-bias the pooled model lacks, below null means participants are more homogeneous than binomial noise.
def test_statistic(df):
    ti = df["trial_index"].astype(int).values
    pid = np.cumsum(np.r_[True, np.diff(ti) != 1])
    d = pd.DataFrame({"pid": pid, "r": df["rating"].astype(float).values, "s": df["number_set"].astype(str).values})
    p = d.groupby("pid").agg(r=("r", "mean"), g=("s", "first"))
    dev = p["r"] - p.groupby("g")["r"].transform("mean")
    return float(np.sqrt(np.mean(dev.values ** 2)))

results.name: largest_gap_fill_vs_other_gaps
results.description: On 3-4 example sets, yes rate for non-example targets lying inside the largest gap between sorted consecutive examples minus those inside the other gaps; observed below null means people fill big gaps between examples less than the single-interval model predicts (clustered/multi-interval generalisation), above null means more.
results.code:
# name: largest_gap_fill_vs_other_gaps
# description: On 3-4 example sets, yes rate for non-example targets lying inside the largest gap between sorted consecutive examples minus those inside the other gaps; observed below null means people fill big gaps between examples less than the single-interval model predicts (clustered/multi-interval generalisation), above null means more.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").values
    n = (~np.isnan(ex)).sum(1)
    srt = np.sort(np.where(np.isnan(ex), np.inf, ex), 1)
    t = df["target"].astype(float).values
    K = srt.shape[1]
    lo = srt[:, :K - 1]; hi = srt[:, 1:]
    with np.errstate(invalid="ignore"):
        gap = np.where(np.isfinite(hi), hi - lo, -1.0)
    big = np.argmax(gap, 1)
    ing = (t[:, None] > lo) & (t[:, None] < hi) & np.isfinite(hi)
    in_any = ing.any(1)
    which = np.argmax(ing, 1)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    m = (n >= 3) & in_any
    a = r[m & (which == big)]; b = r[m & (which != big)]
    if len(a) == 0 or len(b) == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(a.mean() - b.mean())

results.name: adjacent_to_example_yes_rate
results.description: On 2+ example sets, yes rate for non-example targets exactly 1 away from some example minus those 2-5 away from the nearest example; observed above null means immediate numerical neighbours are accepted more than the model's rule/interval mixture predicts (local similarity), below null means neighbours are rejected (e.g. parity breaks) more.
results.code:
# name: adjacent_to_example_yes_rate
# description: On 2+ example sets, yes rate for non-example targets exactly 1 away from some example minus those 2-5 away from the nearest example; observed above null means immediate numerical neighbours are accepted more than the model's rule/interval mixture predicts (local similarity), below null means neighbours are rejected (e.g. parity breaks) more.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").values
    n = (~np.isnan(ex)).sum(1)
    t = df["target"].astype(float).values
    dist = np.nanmin(np.abs(ex - t[:, None]), 1)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    m = n >= 2
    a = r[m & (dist == 1)]; b = r[m & (dist >= 2) & (dist <= 5)]
    if len(a) == 0 or len(b) == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(a.mean() - b.mean())

results.name: endpoint_targets_1_and_100_yes_rate
results.description: Yes rate for targets 1 or 100 when they are not among the examples, minus the yes rate for all other non-example targets in the same sets; observed below null means people reject the scale endpoints more than the model predicts (endpoints as non-outputs), above null means they accept them more.
results.code:
# name: endpoint_targets_1_and_100_yes_rate
# description: Yes rate for targets 1 or 100 when they are not among the examples, minus the yes rate for all other non-example targets in the same sets; observed below null means people reject the scale endpoints more than the model predicts (endpoints as non-outputs), above null means they accept them more.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").values
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values
    isex = (ex == t[:, None]).any(1)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    end = (t == 1) | (t == 100)
    s = df["number_set"].astype(str).values
    sets_with_end = np.unique(s[end & ~isex])
    insets = np.isin(s, sets_with_end) & ~isex
    a = r[insets & end]; b = r[insets & ~end]
    if len(a) == 0 or len(b) == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(a.mean() - b.mean())

results.name: first_vs_last_example_proximity_gap
results.description: On 2+ example sets (target not an example), yes rate when the target is nearer the first-shown example minus when nearer the last-shown example; observed above null means the first example anchors generalisation more than the order-blind model predicts (primacy), below null means recency.
results.code:
# name: first_vs_last_example_proximity_gap
# description: On 2+ example sets (target not an example), yes rate when the target is nearer the first-shown example minus when nearer the last-shown example; observed above null means the first example anchors generalisation more than the order-blind model predicts (primacy), below null means recency.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values
    n = ex.notna().sum(1).values
    first = ex.iloc[:, 0].values
    last = ex.values[np.arange(len(ex)), n - 1]
    isex = (ex.values == t[:, None]).any(1)
    d1 = np.abs(t - first); dl = np.abs(t - last)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    m = (n >= 2) & ~isex
    a = r[m & (d1 < dl)]; b = r[m & (dl < d1)]
    if len(a) == 0 or len(b) == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(a.mean() - b.mean())

results.name: round_target_bonus_with_round_examples
results.description: Among sets containing at least one multiple of 10, yes rate for round targets (multiples of 10, not examples) minus other non-example targets; observed above null means a round example licenses round targets more strongly than the concept model predicts (the converse of the landmark veto), below null means less.
results.code:
# name: round_target_bonus_with_round_examples
# description: Among sets containing at least one multiple of 10, yes rate for round targets (multiples of 10, not examples) minus other non-example targets; observed above null means a round example licenses round targets more strongly than the concept model predicts (the converse of the landmark veto), below null means less.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").values
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values
    has_round = (np.nan_to_num(ex, nan=1) % 10 == 0).any(1)
    isex = (ex == t[:, None]).any(1)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    m = has_round & ~isex
    rd = t % 10 == 0
    a = r[m & rd]; b = r[m & ~rd]
    if len(a) == 0 or len(b) == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(a.mean() - b.mean())

results.name: unsupported_round_inside_vs_outside_range
results.description: Among sets with no multiple of 10, yes rate for round targets inside the examples' [min,max] range minus round targets outside it; observed above null means the round-number doubt is weaker (or confined) within the examples' span than the model's flat veto implies, below null means it is stronger inside the range.
results.code:
# name: unsupported_round_inside_vs_outside_range
# description: Among sets with no multiple of 10, yes rate for round targets inside the examples' [min,max] range minus round targets outside it; observed above null means the round-number doubt is weaker (or confined) within the examples' span than the model's flat veto implies, below null means it is stronger inside the range.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").values
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values
    has_round = (np.nan_to_num(ex, nan=1) % 10 == 0).any(1)
    lo = np.nanmin(ex, 1); hi = np.nanmax(ex, 1)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    m = ~has_round & (t % 10 == 0)
    inside = (t >= lo) & (t <= hi)
    a = r[m & inside]; b = r[m & ~inside]
    if len(a) == 0 or len(b) == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(a.mean() - b.mean())
